history.title: IRS Exchange Fund Ruling Lock

style_when: the story is regulatory or contractual — a filing, a mandate, a rate notice, a certificate, a purchase order that changed the economics
prompt: Overhead flat-lay photograph of a thick, embossed legal financial dossier resting on a dark walnut desk, bound tightly by a heavy, tarnished brass padlock. Shot with a 50mm lens at f/2.8 for a sharp top-down 90-degree view, focusing on the metallic lock texture while the surrounding muted paper tones fall slightly out of focus. Even diffused daylight from a nearby window casts a soft, long shadow across the plain desk surface. One corner of the document is slightly misaligned, suggesting recent handling. Modern, premium, editorial cover standard.
negative_prompt: text, typography, watermark, text, numbers, signature
rationale: This story hinges on a regulatory ruling by the IRS and the resulting contractual lock on financial assets. A document flatlay of a heavy financial filing bound by a physical lock perfectly captures the regulatory closure and the 'seven-year lock' constraint.
subject: a thick, embossed legal dossier bound by a heavy brass lock
core_thesis: The IRS shut down the exchange fund wrapper used to defer taxes on large single-stock positions, effectively locking up concentrated equity under a seven-year rule.
core_conflict: Tax deferral via pooled exchange funds versus strict IRS rules enforcing immediate taxation on concentrated single-stock transfers.
composition: asymmetric top-down framing with the dossier anchored on the lower right third
